column2: Edhamahe (we prosper through devotion to Hari), "pacati" and the like, as before; "bhuyate" and "anubhuyate" are the passive/impersonal forms of the root bhu (verb conjugation).
Bubhushati (desires to be), "bhavayati" (causes to be: "he causes Ishvara to be"); the intensive "bobhuyate" and the intensive-elided "bobhoti" (forms of bhu).
Denominatives "putriyati" (acts like a son), "putrakamyati" (desires a son), "patapatayate"; causative "ghatayati"; desiderative-causative "bubhushayati", and "rupaka" (verb formations).
Optative forms of bhu: "bhavet, bhavetam, bhaveyuh, bhaveh, bhavetam, bhaveta, bhaveyam, bhaveva, bhavema" (optative conjugation).
Optative middle of edh: "edheta, edheyatam, edheran, edhetha, edheyatham, edhedhvam, edheya, edhevahi, edhemahi" ("prospering by mind and fortune").
Imperative of bhu: "astu", "bhavantu", "bhavatat", "bhava", "bhavatam", "bhavata", "bhavani", "bhavava", "bhavama" (imperative conjugation).
Imperative middle: "edhatam, edhetam, edhantam, edhai, pacavahai, pacamahai"; imperfect forms "abhyanandat", "apacatam", "apacan", "apacah" (verb forms).
Imperfect forms: "abhavatam, abhavata, apacam, apacava, apacama"; middle "aidhata, aidhetam, aidhadhvam, aidhe, aidhamahi" (imperfect conjugation).
Aorist (lun): "abhut, abhutam, abhuvan, abhuh, abhuvam"; middle "aidhishta, aidhishatam, aidhishthah, aidhishi" and so on (aorist forms).
Perfect (lit): "babhuva, babhuvatuh, babhuvuh, babhuvitha, babhuvathuh, babhuva, babhuviva, babhuvima" (perfect conjugation of bhu).
Perfect middle of pac and edh: "pece, pecate, pecire", "edhamchakrishe", "edhamchakrathe", "pecidhve", "pece", "pecimahe" (perfect forms).
Periphrastic future (lut): "bhavita, bhavitarau, bhavitarah — Hara and the others"; "bhavitasi, bhavitastha, bhavitasmah — and we ourselves" (future conjugation).
Pakta, paktarau, paktarah; "paktase — you, the auspicious rice"; "paktadhve, paktahe — I"; "paktasmahe — we, Hari's offering of cooked rice" (future of pac).
Benedictive (ashirlin): "May there be happiness: bhuyat; bhuyastam — Hari and Shankara; bhuyasuh; bhuyah; bhuyastam — you two Lords" (blessing forms).
Bhuyasta, bhuyasta yuyam, bhuyasam aham, bhuyasma — always; "yakshishta", "edhishiyastam", "yakshiran", "edhishiya" (benedictive forms).
Yakshivahi, edhishimahi; the conditional (lrin): "ayakshyata, ayakshyetam, ayakshyanta, ayakshye, ayakshyetham — you two" (conditional forms).
Ayakshyadhvam, aidhishyavahi, aidhishyamahi; the simple future (lrit): "syat, bhavishyati, edhishyamahe" and similar (future forms).
So too "vibhavayishyanti", "bobhavishyati" (intensive); "ghatayet", "patayet"; likewise "putriyati" and "kamyati" (further verbal formations).
With the suffix ktin: "vriddhi", "stuti", "mati"; with ghan: "bhava"; with yuc: "karana", "bhavana" and the like; with a: "chikitsa" (formation of action nouns).
Likewise the gerundives in tavya and aniya: "kartavya", "karaniya"; "deya", "dhyeya"; with yat and nyat: "karya", "kritya" (verbal derivatives).

Ktadi suffixes (past participles) are known to denote the agent, and sometimes the action or object: "gato gramam" (gone to the village), "gato gramah", "alishtash cha gurus tvaya" (the teacher embraced by you).
Present participles shatri and shanach: "bhavan" (being), "edhamanah"; "bhavantyapi"; the suffixes vun and trich added to all roots: "bhavaka" (one who causes to be), "bhavita" (one who will be).
Forms ending in kvip, such as "svayambhu"; the perfect participles in kvasu and kana: "babhuvivan", "pecivan", "pecanah", "shraddadhanaka" (perfect participles).
With the suffix an: "kumbhakara" (potter) and the like; with the Unadi suffixes also in the past sense: "vayu", "payu", "karu" — and in the Veda the usage is varied (Unadi derivations).
Lightning: "tadit, saudamini, vidyut, chanchala, chapala"; "sphurjathu" is the thunder-crash, "vajranishpesha" the thunderbolt; "vrishtighata" is a break in the rain, "avagraha" a drought.
Dhara (downpour), "sampata", "ashara" (heavy shower), "shikara" and "ambukana" (spray, drops of water); "varshopala" is hail; "durdina" is a day clouded over by rain.
Antardha, "vyavadha" (masculine); "antardhi", "apavarana" (concealment); "apidhana", "tirodhana", "pidhana", "chhadana" (covering).
Moon: "abja, jaivatrika, soma, glau, mriganka, kalanidhi, vidhu, kumudabandhu"; "bimba" (disc, neuter), "mandala" (circle, in all genders).
Kala is the sixteenth part (of the moon); "bhitta", "shakala", "khandaka" are a fragment; "chandrika, kaumudi, jyotsna" are moonlight; "prasada" is clarity, serenity.
Lakshana, lakshmaka, chihna (mark, sign); "shobha, kanti, dyuti, chhavi" (beauty, lustre); "sushama, parama shobha"; "tushara, tuhina, hima" (frost, snow).
Avashyaya, nihara (mist); "praleya, shishira, hima" (dew, cold); "nakshatra, riksha, bha, tara, taraka, udu" (star; "udu" also feminine).
Jupiter: "guru, jiva, angirasa"; Venus: "ushana, bhargava, kavi"; "vidhuntuda, tamas, rahu" is the eclipse-planet; "lagna" is the rising of a zodiac sign.
The seven sages: Marichi, Atri, and the others; "chitrashikhandin" (the bright-crested ones); the sun: "haridashva, brahma, pusha, dyumani, mihira, ravi" (names of the sun).
Parivesha and "paridhi" are the halo; "upasuryaka" and "bhandala" are other terms for it; rays: "kirana, asramayukha, amshu, gabhasti, ghrini, dhrishni".
Bhanu, kara, marichi (ray), "didhiti" (feminine); "prabha, ruk, ruchi, tvish, bha, bhas, chhavi, dyuti, dipti" (radiance).
Rochis and "shochis" (neuter); "prakasha, dyota, atapa" (light, sunshine); "koshna, kavoshna, mandoshna, kaduṣhna" (lukewarm, mildly hot) are used of what is hot.
Tigma, tikshna, khara (sharp, fierce); "dishta" and "kalaka"; "ghasra" (day), "dinaha"; "sayam-sandhya" (evening twilight), "pitriprasu" (the evening, mother of the ancestors).
Pratyusha (dawn), "aharmukha", "kalya", "usha"; the periods "prahna" (forenoon), "aparahna" (afternoon), "madhyahna" (midday); "trisandhya" (three twilights); then "sharvari" (night).
Yami, tami, tamisra (night), "jyotsni" (moonlit night); "pakshini" is a night joined to the preceding and following days (as in "agami", "vartamana" days).
Ardharatra, nishitha (midnight), "pradosha" (evening), "rajanimukha"; "parvasandhi" is the junction between the fifteenth and first lunar days.
Pakshanta are the two fifteenth tithis; "paurnamasi" and "purnima" mean the full moon; "anumati" when a digit is lacking, "raka" when the moon is full.
Amavasya and "amavasya" (new moon), "darsha" is the conjunction of sun and moon; "sinivali" when the moon is just seen, "kuhu" when the moon's digit is lost.
Samvarta, pralaya, kalpa, kshaya, kalpanta (dissolution, end of an aeon); "kalusha, vrijina, ena, agha, amhas, duritam, dushkrita" (sin, evil deed).
Dharma (neuter, masculine); "punya, shreyas, sukrita, vrisha" (merit); "mud, priti, pramada, harsha, pramoda, amoda, sammada" (joy).
Ananda, anandathu, shama, sharma, shata, sukha (happiness); "shvah-shreyasa, shiva, bhadra, kalyana, mangala, shubha" (auspicious, good).
Bhavuka, bhavika, bhavya, kushala, kshema (welfare), neuter; "daiva, dishta, magadheya, bhagya" (fate); "niyati" and "vidhi" are feminine words for destiny.
Kshetrajna, atma, purusha (the knower of the field, the Self, the Person); "pradhana, prakriti" (feminine); "hetu" (masculine), "karana, bija, nidana, adikarana" (cause).
Chitta, chetas, hridaya, svanta, hrid, manas (heart, mind); "buddhi, manisha, dhishana, dhi, prajna, shemushi, mati" (intellect).
Preksha, upalabdhi, chit, samvit, pratipat, jnapti, chetana (perception, awareness); "dhi, dharana, medha" (retention, intelligence); "sankalpa" is a mental act.
Sankhya (reckoning), "vicharana, charcha" (deliberation, discussion), "vichikitsa, samshaya" (doubt); "adhyahara, tarka, uha" (inference, conjecture); "nirnaya, nishchaya" (decision).
Mithyadrishti, nastikata (false view, unbelief), "bhranti, mithyamati, bhrama" (error); "angikara, abhyupagama, pratishrava, samadhi" (assent, promise).
In liberation the word is "dhi" (wisdom) and "jnana"; elsewhere "vijnana" is knowledge of crafts and treatises; "mukti, kaivalya, nirvana, shreyas, nihshreyasa, amrita" (liberation).
Moksha, apavarga (liberation); then ignorance: "ajnana, avidya, ahammati" (feminine; self-conceit); "parimala" is fragrance rising from crushing, a scent pleasing to people.
Amoda is a far-reaching fragrance; "surabhi" gratifies the nose; whites: "shukla, shubhra, shuchi, shveta, vishada, shveta, pandara" (white).
Avadata, sita, gaura, valaksha, dhavala, arjuna (white); "harina, pandura, pandu" (pale, whitish); "pandu" slightly; "dhusara" (dusky).
Black: "nila, asita, shyama, kala, shyamala, mecha(ka)"; yellow: "pita, gaura, haridrabha, palasha"; green: "harita, harit".
Red: "rohita, lohita, rakta, shona" (the lotus-hued "kokanadachhavi"); "aruna" is a faintly marked red; "patala" is red mixed with white (pink).
Shyava (dark brown), "kapisha" (tawny), "dhumra, dhumala" (smoky), "krishnalohita" (dark red); "kadara, kapila, pinga, pishanga, kadrupingala" (shades of brown-yellow).
Chitra, kirmira, kalmasha, shabala, karbura (variegated, spotted); then speech: "vyahara, ukti, lapita" (utterance); "apabhramsha, apashabda" (corrupt speech).
A word complete with verbal and nominal endings is poetry, or an action with its factors; "itihasa" is ancient narrative; "purana" has five characteristics.
Akhyayika (tale), "upalabdhartha", "prabandha" (composition), "kalpana", "katha" (story); "samahara, sangraha" (collection); "pravahlika, prahelika" (riddle).
Samasya is an abridged meaning; "smriti" is a code of law (dharma-samhita); "akhya, ahva, abhidhana" (name); "varta, vrittanta" (news, narrative).
Huti, akarana, ahvana (calling, summoning); "upanyasa" and "vanmukha" (introduction); "vivada, vyavahara" is a dispute, a case at law, with "prativakya" the reply and "uttara" the answer.
Upodghata, udahara (introduction, example); "artha, mithyabhisamshana" (false accusation); "abhishapa" (curse); "yasha, kirti" (fame); "prashna, prichchha, anuyoga" (question).
Amredita is the doubled or tripled utterance (also in contempt, blame, reproach); "abhashana, alapa" (address, conversation); "pralapa" is meaningless speech.
Anulapa (repeated speech), "volapa", "paridevana" (lament); "vipralapa" (contradictory speech); "samlapa, bhashana" (mutual conversation).
Supralapa, suvachana (fair speech); "apalapa, nihnava" (denial); "ushati" is gentle but unwholesome speech; "sangata, hridayangama" (agreeable, heart-reaching).
Saugandhika, kahlara (white water-lily), "nilam, indivara, kaja" (blue lotus); "utpala, kuvalaya"; "kumuda, kairava" (white night-lotus).
Shaluka is their tuber; "padma, tamarasa, sankaja" (lotus); "nilotpala, kuvalaya" (blue lotus); "rakta, kokanada" (red lotus).
Karahata, shipha, kanda (tuber), "kinjalka, kesara" (filament, neuter); "khani, akara" (mine, feminine); "padah" are foothills, "pratyantaparvata" the border mountains.
Upatyaka is the land near a mountain, "adhityaka" the land above it. The groups beginning with heaven and the nether world have been told; now hear the words of many meanings.
Nama (indeed; in manifestation, possibility, anger, approach, contempt); "alam" (adornment, sufficiency, capacity, prohibition) — indeclinables and their senses.
Hum (in doubt, in questioning); "samaya" (near, middle); "punar" (again, not first, difference); "nir/nis" (certainty, negation) — particles and their meanings.
Syat (in composition); "chirati" (long past); "purā" (formerly, also of what is about to come); "urari, uri, orari" (in extension, assent — three words).
Kila (in heaven, the other world, hearsay, uncertainty); "khalu" (in prohibition, as an ornament of speech, in inquiry, on occasion) — indeclinables and their meanings.
